decision-tree.root-question: Is a decision being made on a live incident bridge right now (mitigation, rollback, release hold, traffic shift)?

branch.conclusion: Skip this methodology. A retrospective write-up belongs in the postmortem; a planned change belongs in an ADR, not an incident decision record.

branch.question: Is the bridge still open, so the record can be written within 2 minutes of the call?

branch.conclusion: Write the record now but mark it `reconstructed: true` with the reconstruction time; raise the missing scribe in the postmortem.

branch.question: Does the decision name a rollback trigger as metric + threshold + window + rollback command?

branch.conclusion: Stop and agree the numeric trigger on the bridge before the mitigation ships; record it in `inputs[]` as `rollback_trigger`.

branch.question: Are `blast_radius` (with a number) and `options_considered` (at least two, including do-nothing) both recorded?

branch.conclusion: Fill `blast_radius` from the open dashboard and list the rejected options; then commit.
Commit the record with the commander as owner, pinned evidence and `review.next_review_at` set to the postmortem date.

example.p: Live bridge, 02:14. Commander decides to disable the recommendations sidecar. Rollback trigger agreed as "checkout 5xx above 2% for 5 min; `helm rollback checkout 41`"; blast radius recorded as 38% of checkout requests in eu-west-1; options: disable sidecar / roll back full release / wait 10 min. All present → run-the-checklist; record committed 02:16.
